svg.text: WHO uses the system, and for WHAT goals. No order, no steps.
Actor: a role outside the system: a person (Customer) or a system (Spoolman).
Use case: a goal, named verb + noun ("Place order"). Not a function or a step.
Association: plain solid line. The actor takes part in that use case.
System boundary (box with the system's name)
«include»: dashed arrow, open head, FROM the base use case TO the
part that ALWAYS happens inside it.
«extend»: dashed arrow FROM an optional extra TO the base use case.
Common mistakes: arrows between actors and use cases; use cases as steps.
The STEPS of one process, in order, with choices and parallel work.
one thing that is done ("Check input")
each outgoing arrow gets a guard: [valid] / [invalid]
fork splits into parallel flows, join waits for all
Swimlanes: columns that show WHO does each action.
Common mistakes: decisions without guards; a fork with no join.
MESSAGES between objects over time, for ONE scenario. Time runs downward.
Lifeline: box + dashed line. One per object or system taking part.
Message: solid line, filled arrowhead (a call / request).
Return: dashed line, open arrowhead (the answer).
Frames: alt = if/else, opt = if, loop = repeat. Conditions in [ ].
Common mistakes: missing returns; time going upward;
The STRUCTURE: the important classes, their data and how they relate.
is made of; the part dies with the whole
has; the part can live on its own
"is a"; arrow points to the parent class
uses it briefly (e.g. as an argument)
Common mistakes: every helper class included;
arrows without multiplicity; mixing up the two diamonds.
